analysis:
The only change in EngineV2Bridge+Submission.swift is at base line 249 / head 249-250: EngineV2Translation.cbv2Request now also receives `stopStringScope: stopStringScope`. The new argument is not defined in the visible base text. In the supplied evidence, submitTokenized has no `stopStringScope` parameter, so it presumably resolves to a bridge property or a new parameter added elsewhere in the PR. I could not see that definition, the EngineV2Translation.cbv2Request signature change, or how the value is derived and consumed.

Relevant surfaces: T-041 and TB-007 (prefix-cache scope, stop-string handling); A-001 (consumer prompt confidentiality). The visible code already routes cacheScope and checkpointCacheSalt from authenticated coordinator metadata (lines 242, 253). Stop strings are used downstream at line 937 (`stopSequences: cbv2Request.stopStrings`) for output truncation in runPump.

The changed context shows no weakening of cache scoping, TTL, HMAC lookup names or the SSD path. The hunk does not alter admission, deadline, KV reservation or cleanup. Whether stopStringScope influences cache keying (for example whether a cache key now depends on stop-string state), whether it could be attacker-influenced, and whether it is bounded in size, cannot be verified from this unit.

Next-pass questions: (1) where stopStringScope is defined and its trust origin (coordinator-authenticated vs request-supplied); (2) whether it feeds the cache salt or checkpoint scope, and if so whether the scope isolation in T-041 is preserved; (3) whether the stop-string implementation bounds length, count and memory (DoS, T-029/T-010). No concrete regression is supported by the visible evidence.
